subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: The Annunciation
overview: The annunciation is the announcement of the birth of Jesus Christ. In Luke 1:26-37 the angel Gabriel tells Mary that she will give birth to Jesus. In this sub-strand you will narrate that event, see why His birth is unique, recite Luke 1:37, and learn from Mary's holy life.

lessons.title: The angel's message to Mary
objectives: Narrate the annunciation from Luke 1:26-37 in order.
Name the people in the account and the message about Jesus.
lessons.intro: Good news is sometimes brought by a messenger. God sent the angel Gabriel to a young woman in Nazareth with the news that she would be the mother of Jesus.
lessons.notes:
Annunciation means an announcement. This announcement is the birth of Jesus Christ. Read Luke 1:26-37 in turns and narrate only what those verses say.

### The visit
In the sixth month of Elizabeth's pregnancy, God sent the angel Gabriel to Nazareth, a town in Galilee. He went to a virgin named Mary. She was pledged to be married to Joseph, a descendant of David. The angel said, "Greetings, you who are highly favoured! The Lord is with you."

Mary was greatly troubled and wondered what kind of greeting this was. The angel told her not to be afraid. She had found favour with God. She would conceive and give birth to a son, and she must name Him Jesus.

### Who the child would be
The angel said Jesus would be great and would be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God would give Him the throne of His father David. He would reign over Jacob's descendants forever. His kingdom would never end.

### Mary's question
Mary asked how this could be, since she was a virgin. The angel answered that the Holy Spirit would come upon her and the power of the Most High would overshadow her. The holy one to be born would be called the Son of God. The angel also said that Elizabeth, Mary's relative, was going to have a child in her old age, and that she was already in her sixth month. Luke 1:37 says that no word from God will ever fail. With God, nothing is impossible.

When you narrate, keep this order: Gabriel sent to Mary in Nazareth; the greeting; her trouble; the name Jesus; the throne of David and the kingdom that never ends; her question; the Holy Spirit; Elizabeth; the promise that God's word does not fail.

keyWords.meaning: the announcement of the birth of Jesus Christ
a person who has not had sexual relations; Luke 1:27 describes Mary in this way
the angel God sent to Mary

activity.title: Read and role-play the annunciation
steps: Role-play the annunciation: Gabriel, Mary, and a narrator.
If a video clip of the annunciation is available, watch it and say which parts match the reading.
In groups, retell the announcement in the correct order.

practice.question: Who brought the announcement to Mary, and where did she live?
practice.answer: The angel Gabriel came to Mary in Nazareth in Galilee.

practice.question: What name was Mary to give the child, and whose throne would He receive?
practice.answer: She was to name Him Jesus. God would give Him the throne of His father David.

practice.question: How did the angel say Mary would conceive, since she was a virgin?
practice.answer: The Holy Spirit would come upon her, and the power of the Most High would overshadow her.

summary: Gabriel announced to Mary in Nazareth that she would give birth to Jesus.
Jesus would be the Son of the Most High, and His kingdom would never end.
Mary was a virgin. The child would be conceived by the Holy Spirit.

lessons.title: A unique birth and Luke 1:37
objectives: Explain why the birth of Jesus Christ is unique.
Recite Luke 1:37 and say what it means to trust God's power.
lessons.intro: Many children are born into families. The birth announced to Mary is different from every other birth. Luke 1:37 tells us why such a thing could be promised.
lessons.notes:
Unique means one of a kind. The birth of Jesus is unique for reasons that Luke 1:26-37 itself gives.

### Why this birth is unique
- Mary was a virgin. She said so to the angel.
- The child would be conceived by the Holy Spirit, not in the ordinary way.
- He would be called the Son of the Most High and the Son of God.
- He would sit on David's throne and reign forever. His kingdom would never end.
- The announcement came from God through the angel Gabriel, not from a human plan.

No other baby in the passage is described in this way. Elizabeth's child was a wonderful gift in her old age, and the angel used that gift as a sign. Jesus' birth is still different, because He is the Son of God.

### Luke 1:37
The verse teaches that nothing is impossible with God. His word does not fail. Mary could trust the promise because of who God is, not because she could see how a virgin would bear a child.

Recite the verse: "For there is nothing that God cannot do." Meditate on it. Sit quietly and think of one thing that seems too hard for you. Then remember that God's power is greater than that hard thing. Trust means depending on Him.

### Trust in daily life
You trust God's power when you pray about a sick relative, a fear, or a problem you cannot fix. You also work and obey. Trust is not laziness. It is refusing to believe that God is too weak to keep His word. The annunciation happened because God's word does not fail.

keyWords.meaning: to depend on God's power and His word
something people cannot do; Luke 1:37 says it is not impossible for God

activity.title: Recite and meditate on Luke 1:37
steps: Write Luke 1:37 on a flash card.
Recite it together, then meditate quietly on God's power.
In groups, list the facts that make the birth of Jesus unique.
Sing a song about the annunciation of the birth of Jesus Christ.

practice.question: Give two reasons why the birth of Jesus is unique.
practice.answer: Any two: Mary was a virgin; He was conceived by the Holy Spirit; He is the Son of God; His kingdom will never end; the angel Gabriel announced Him.

practice.question: What does Luke 1:37 teach?
practice.answer: Nothing is impossible with God. His word does not fail.

practice.question: How can a learner trust God's power?
practice.answer: By praying, depending on His word, and remembering that God can do what people cannot do.

summary: Jesus' birth is unique because He was conceived by the Holy Spirit and is the Son of God.
Luke 1:37: nothing is impossible with God.

lessons.title: Learning from Mary's holy life
objectives: Describe Mary's response as a holy example.
Explain why sexual purity matters for young people.
lessons.intro: Mary was highly favoured, and she was a virgin pledged to Joseph. Young Christians are asked to emulate her by leading a holy life.
lessons.notes:
To emulate means to copy a good example. Mary is the mother of Jesus. Luke 1:26-37 shows her as a virgin who listened to God, asked an honest question, and heard that the Holy Spirit would do what people cannot do. She did not laugh at the angel. She did not treat God's message lightly.

### A holy life
Holy means set apart for God. Mary's life, as this passage presents it, was pure. She was pledged to be married, and she had kept herself a virgin. Christians honour that purity.

For a Grade 4 learner, leading a holy life means:

- Obeying God at home and at school.
- Keeping your body pure and saying no to sexual talk, pictures and touching that are wrong.
- Waiting until marriage for sex. That is abstinence, and it is part of holiness.
- Dressing neatly and respecting other people's bodies.
- Telling the truth and being kind, because holiness is more than one rule.
- Praying when you are tempted.

### Why sexual purity is important
God made our bodies as something precious. Sex is for marriage, not for childhood. Purity protects you from harm, from shame and from choices that are hard to undo. It also honours the God who sent Gabriel to a pure young woman. Say clearly in class why purity matters, using respectful words.

You emulate Mary when you trust God's word, as Luke 1:37 teaches, and when you keep your life clean for Him. Sing about the annunciation, and ask God for a holy heart.

keyWords.meaning: a life set apart for God and kept pure
keeping yourself clean in body and behaviour, including saying no to sex before marriage

activity.title: Why purity is important
steps: Read Luke 1:27 and 1:34 again and note that Mary was a virgin.
In groups, say why sexual purity is important, using respectful language.
Each learner says one way to emulate Mary this week.
Sing a song about the annunciation.

practice.question: How is Mary an example of a holy life in Luke 1:26-37?
practice.answer: She was a virgin who listened to God's message and trusted what the angel said about the Holy Spirit.

practice.question: Give two ways a learner can lead a holy life.
practice.answer: Any two: obey God, keep the body pure, say no to wrong touching and bad pictures, wait until marriage for sex, pray when tempted, tell the truth.

summary: Mary listened to God as a virgin highly favoured.
Young Christians emulate her by living a holy and pure life.
Sexual purity means keeping sex for marriage and saying no to what is wrong.

quiz.question: The annunciation is...
options: the announcement of the birth of Jesus
quiz.explanation: Annunciation means the announcement Gabriel brought to Mary.

quiz.question: God sent the angel Gabriel to Mary in...
quiz.explanation: Luke 1:26 says Gabriel was sent to Nazareth in Galilee.

quiz.question: Mary was pledged to marry...
quiz.explanation: Luke 1:27 names Joseph, a descendant of David.

quiz.question: The child was to be named...
quiz.explanation: Luke 1:31 says Mary must name Him Jesus.

quiz.question: Which fact shows that the birth of Jesus is unique?
options: He would be conceived by the Holy Spirit and called the Son of God
He was born in the ordinary way with no promise
The angel said the kingdom would end quickly
quiz.explanation: Luke 1:34-35 gives the virgin birth by the Holy Spirit and the title Son of God.

quiz.question: His kingdom would...
quiz.explanation: Luke 1:33 says His kingdom will never end.

quiz.question: Luke 1:37 teaches that...
quiz.answer: Nothing is impossible with God. His word does not fail.
quiz.explanation: The verse is the reason Mary could trust the promise.

quiz.question: Trusting God's power means...
options: hiding from every problem without prayer
quiz.explanation: Luke 1:37 is recited so learners trust God's power.

quiz.question: To emulate Mary means...
quiz.explanation: Emulate means to follow a good example. Mary is the example of a holy life.

quiz.question: Why is sexual purity important for a young Christian?
quiz.answer: Because God wants a holy life, the body is precious, and sex is for marriage, not for childhood.
quiz.explanation: The sub-strand links Mary's example with abstinence and holiness.
